title: Robust Conditional Conformal Prediction via Branched Normalizing Flow
claim: Marginal coverage hides conditional failures under shift; bounding the gap by Wasserstein distance motivates an invertible two-branch flow that restores conditional validity.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right (Challenge, Theory, Method), stacked sub-diagrams, arrows linking steps
description: Three bordered panels titled (a) Challenge, (b) Theory and (c) Method, read left to right. Panel (a) shows scatter plots of orange calibration and green test samples with a gray constant-width band, then a CDF plot with a small marginal gap. A red-crossed arrow leads to a scatter with an adaptive orange band that fails on shifted green points, labeled 'Unreliable Conditional Coverage'. Panel (b) has a 3D CDF surface, a zoomed CCG plot with a bracket, density curves feeding an integral for ICG, and nested green and orange contour shapes joined by blue Wasserstein transport arrows. Panel (c) shows the BNF with x and y branches in blue and red boxes. Below it, a scatter shows Step 1 (normalize) and Step 2 (inverse transform), with density-curve insets in red and blue rounded boxes. The eye goes first to the colorful scatter and band plots.
caption: (a) Vanilla prediction set CM(x) has constant size and offers marginal coverage, which is robust if conformal score distributions PV and QV have similar cumulative probabilities at τ. Conditional prediction set CC(x) has input-dependent size and provides conditional guarantees for calibration inputs Xi = x where i = 1, ..., n, but may fail on non-i.i.d. test input Xn+1 = x. The difference between PV and QV can not capture the reliability of conditional coverage on the shifted test data; (b) Conditional coverage gap (CCG) measures CC(Xn+1) validity at x by comparing PV |X=x and QV |X=x. Integrated coverage gap (ICG) is the expectation of CCG under QX for a holistic robustness measure. Wasserstein distance W(PXY , QXY ) bounds ICG to reveal how a distribution shift results in non-i.i.d. conformal scores. abstract: Conformal prediction (CP) constructs prediction sets with marginal coverage guarantees under the assumption that the calibration and test distributions are identical. However, under distribution shift, existing approaches primarily align marginal conformal score distributions, which is sufficient to preserve marginal coverage but does not control the conditional coverage error at individual test inputs. As a consequence, CP can remain unreliable in regions where the conditional score distributions are mismatched. In this work, we bound the conditional invalidity of CP under distribution shift in terms of the Wasserstein distance between the calibration and test distributions. This result highlights the role of invertible transport in mitigating conditional coverage degradation. Motivated by this insight, we introduce Branched Normalizing Flow (BNF), a two-branch architecture that normalizes a test input to the calibration distribution and transforms the prediction set of the normalized input back to the test distribution while preserving conditional guarantees. Empirically, BNF consistently improves conditional coverage robustness on nine datasets across a wide range of confidence levels.
